## File Fitted Card (FF)

The parent-sized collection cell, and **the format most often prerendered**.

### It queries the host's container and refuses to make its own

Layout is driven entirely by the host's `fitted-card` size container. This shell queries that container and **deliberately does not create a competing one**.

That single decision is why a grid tile, a list strip and a badge-height row each get a composition that *fits*, rather than a scaled-down copy of one design. A shell that declared `container-type: size` itself would shadow the host's container and every cell would size against its own box instead of the slot it was given.

### The budgets are applied before this component ever sees the data

Truncated text, capped rows and entries, resampled waveforms — all of it happens in `fileViewModel` at projection time, not here. By the time the fitted shell renders, the payload is already bounded.

This matters for anyone extending a family renderer: **do not add a budget in the component**. If a fitted cell is showing too much, the projection is what needs fixing, and fixing it there keeps the prerender path bounded too.

### The family this belongs to

Five pieces make up how a file renders in Boxel:

| Piece | Job |
|---|---|
| `file-shell-atom` | inline reference — icon, name, extension |
| `file-shell-embedded` | complete content, flowing inside a document |
| `file-shell-fitted` | the parent-sized collection cell |
| `file-shell-isolated` | the full work surface |
| `file-preview-stage` | the slot all four project into; owns loading, failure, provenance |

A shell never knows how to draw a PDF, a waveform or a 3D scene. It renders the
stage, and the stage hands the remaining space to the family's own renderer,
declared by a FileDef subclass as `static previewComponent`. A file whose family
has no renderer yet gets an honest generic pane rather than a broken one.
